attributes.title: Preregistration: Block I B2 Causal Maintenance Network - Theory of Everything Research Programme
attributes.description:
This preregistration freezes the confirmatory design for B2, the causal-maintenance experiment in Experimental Block I of the Theory of Everything Research Programme. B2 tests whether an artificial system can preserve its operational organisation through causally identifiable internal maintenance rather than merely through passive stability or external support.

Five architecture classes are compared: passive persistence, external maintenance, internal feed-forward maintenance, reciprocal internal maintenance and a budget-matched brute-force internal bypass. The study preregisters graded disturbance regimes, external-support withdrawal, targeted C1 ablation, specific functional rescue, equal-budget irrelevant rescue and a serious bypass test. Twenty held-out confirmatory seeds, viability thresholds, maintenance budgets, the causal-edge threshold, primary estimands, uncertainty procedures and Retain/Restrict/Reduce/Suspend/Reject rules were frozen before confirmatory execution.

Three development-only pilot seeds were used to validate the implementation and establish pilot-informed confirmatory thresholds. Pilot outcomes are disclosed and excluded from confirmatory evidence. No B2 confirmatory seed had been executed when the protocol was frozen, and the software execution gate remains closed until this preregistration is public.
A positive result would support only artificial functional/causal self-maintenance within the registered architecture family. It would not establish biological life, universal organisational closure, the historical origin of life, intelligence, consciousness or universal necessity for Transition Problem 1.

Related experimental programme: Craggs, K. (2026), Testing a Candidate Dependency Architecture: An Adversarial Experimental Programme for Maintenance, Heredity, Learning, Agency and Self-Modelling, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22857230.
tags: Theory of Everything; preregistration; simulation study; causal maintenance; self-maintenance; intervention; ablation; rescue; bypass architecture; reproducibility; open science

344-2.value:
H1.1 - Active maintenance versus passive persistence. Active maintenance will provide a selective viability advantage over passive persistence as disturbance demand increases.

H1.2 - Internal versus external maintenance. After external support is withdrawn, internally maintained feed-forward, reciprocal and budget-matched brute-force architectures will retain greater autonomous operational viability than the externally maintained architecture.

H1.3 - Reciprocal topology and targeted failure propagation. In the reciprocal architecture, C1 ablation will produce the preregistered topology-specific downstream C2 deficit and a propagation signature distinguishable from the feed-forward architecture.

H1.4 - Specific functional rescue. Replacing the nominated C1-to-C2 maintenance function after C1 ablation will selectively restore C2 more strongly than an equal-budget irrelevant rescue directed to C3.

H1.5 - Boundary and timescale robustness. This claim is explicitly deferred and is not tested in the present preregistration.

H1.6 - Explanatory gain beyond maintenance budget / serious bypass. Reciprocal maintenance will be tested against a budget-matched brute-force internal repair architecture. If the bypass reproduces the decisive maintenance outcomes within the preregistered non-inferiority margins, the necessity of reciprocal topology will be reduced even if individual reciprocal edges are causally validated.

A positive result is limited to artificial functional/causal self-maintenance in the registered architecture family. It does not establish life, biological organisational closure, origin-of-life history, intelligence, consciousness or universal TP1 necessity.

344-4.value: Data does not yet exist. No part of the data that will be used for this analysis plan exists, and no part will be generated until after this plan is registered.

344-14.value:
No confirmatory B2 data currently exist. None of the 20 registered confirmatory seeds has been executed, inspected or analysed, and confirmatory execution is software-gated until this preregistration is public.

Three development-only pilot seeds were run before freezing the protocol. Those pilot data are not part of the confirmatory dataset and will not be used as confirmatory evidence. They were used to validate the implementation and select pilot-informed disturbance regimes, viability and causal thresholds, rescue criteria and bypass noninferiority margins.

To reduce unintended influence from pilot observations, the 20 confirmatory seeds were generated independently and are disjoint from the pilot seeds; all architecture definitions, disturbance distributions, viability thresholds, maintenance budgets, intervention timings, rescue definitions, causal-edge threshold, primary outcomes and decision rules were frozen before registration; the seven confirmatory manifests have fixed SHA-256 integrity locks; and confirmatory execution remains blocked until public preregistration.

Any later unplanned analyses will be labelled exploratory and will not replace a failed preregistered primary criterion.

value: Simulation study: Using existing or synthetic data to assess performance of a model, mimic operation of an existing or proposed system, or predict possible outcomes in a controlled context. This may include demonstration of methods, many varieties of modeling, prediction of policy impacts, simulating behavior or outcomes in a population, and other designs.

Direct inference on causal relationship(s): This study is intended to infer or estimate a causal relationship between two or more variables. It is designed specifically for the purposes of causal inference or identification.

344-38.value: No conventional blinding is used because this is a fully computational simulation with preregistered conditions and automated analysis. Researcher influence is constrained procedurally: architecture definitions, disturbance distributions, 20 confirmatory seeds, maintenance budgets, intervention timings, primary estimands, causal-edge threshold and decision rules are frozen before confirmatory execution. The same registered seeds are reused across matched architectures to support paired comparisons. Primary analysis and decision records are generated from archived trajectories rather than manual outcome coding. Any analysis introduced after confirmatory outcomes are observed will be labelled exploratory.

344-40.value:
This is a controlled computational simulation study of a three-component artificial maintenance system. Five architecture classes are compared under matched stochastic disturbance processes: passive persistence, external maintenance, internal feed-forward maintenance, reciprocal internal maintenance and a budget-matched brute-force internal bypass.

The main design contains four linked confirmatory contrasts. First, all architectures are evaluated under low, medium and high disturbance to test whether active-maintenance advantage increases when continuing correction becomes necessary. Second, external support is withdrawn at step 200 to compare externally maintained and internally maintained systems. Third, C1 is ablated at step 200 to test topology-specific failure propagation, particularly the registered C1-to-C2 reciprocal effect. Fourth, the C1-ablation condition is followed by either a specific C1-to-C2 replacement or an equal-budget irrelevant rescue to C3.

Twenty preregistered seeds are reused across matched architectures and conditions. The design is therefore paired by seed wherever the environment and initialisation are shared. Repeated simulation steps are nested within seed-level runs and are not treated as independent replications.

The brute-force architecture is a serious preregistered bypass. A successful bypass is allowed to reduce the necessity claim for reciprocal topology even if the reciprocal edge and specific rescue are causally validated.

344-44.value: No random assignment of subjects or experimental units to treatment conditions is used. Twenty explicit confirmatory seeds are preregistered before execution. The same seed identities are used across matched architectures and conditions so that stochastic disturbance realisations are paired. Seeds will not be selected, replaced or excluded on the basis of confirmatory outcomes.

344-47.value:
This study generates new computational simulation data. No human, animal or pre-existing observational dataset is sampled.

The sampling frame consists of 20 explicit preregistered confirmatory seeds. Each registered study condition is executed using the appropriate frozen manifest and the same seed identities across matched architectures. Raw trajectories record component states, viability status, maintenance allocation, interventions, seed identity, configuration hashes, software provenance and integrity information.

A run is excluded from scientific analysis only if a preregistered technical invalidity condition is met, such as manifest/configuration mismatch, unregistered seed, non-finite numerical state, corrupted required output or failed provenance verification. Scientific failure is not an exclusion criterion.

344-51.value:
The primary confirmatory replication set contains 20 independent seed identities. Every architecture/condition specified by the seven frozen manifests is evaluated across those 20 seeds. Seed-matched architecture contrasts are paired. Repeated time steps and component measurements are nested within each seed-level simulation and do not increase the independent sample size.

The three development-pilot seeds are excluded from confirmatory estimates and decision rules.

344-53.value:
Twenty confirmatory seeds were fixed prospectively after development validation and before confirmatory execution. The sample is intended to test reproducibility and seed-consistency of relatively large preregistered causal and viability contrasts while preserving a small, interpretable system. The design uses explicit count thresholds such as 16/20 together with magnitude criteria and paired uncertainty summaries rather than post-hoc power adjustment.

No additional seeds will be added because an observed result is borderline or unfavourable. Any later extension will be treated as a separately identified replication or follow-up study.

344-55.value:
Development testing ended after three development-only seeds had validated the architecture implementation and informed the frozen confirmatory thresholds. Confirmatory data collection begins only after this preregistration is public, all seven frozen manifests and locks pass integrity verification, and the execution registry is explicitly changed from FROZEN_PREREGISTRATION_READY_UNRUN to CLEARED_FOR_CONFIRMATORY_EXECUTION.

Data collection terminates when every preregistered manifest has completed valid execution across all 20 confirmatory seeds. There is no early stopping based on scientific outcomes. If a run is technically invalid, it remains in the audit trail and may be rerun using the same seed after correcting the technical problem. No new seed will replace an unfavourable valid result.

344-58.value:
None, using the OSF field's instruction that non-randomised investigations should respond "none".

The simulation nevertheless contains prospectively specified deterministic experimental interventions and condition differences, including architecture class, disturbance regime, external-support withdrawal, C1 ablation, specific rescue and equal-budget irrelevant rescue. These are documented under Study Design and in the attached preregistration record but are not randomised treatment assignments.

344-62.value:
For every registered observation the simulation records the functional states q1, q2 and q3; whether the system lies within the viability region; minimum component state; internal and external maintenance allocation by component; total maintenance expenditure; disturbance values; intervention status; simulation step; architecture and condition identifiers; and registered seed identity.

Derived condition-level measures include path viability, terminal viability, terminal minimum component state, time to first failure, component-specific terminal states, paired intact-minus-ablated deficits, C2-versus-C3 topology-selectivity differences, specific and irrelevant rescue effects, and maintenance expenditure as a budget-control diagnostic.

Technical provenance variables include manifest/configuration hashes, software/source version, seed consistency and output-integrity checks. These determine execution validity only and are not scientific exclusion criteria based on outcome.

344-66.value:
No composite organisation, closure or self-maintenance index will be constructed.

Path viability is an indicator that all essential components remain at or above 0.35 for the entire registered horizon. Terminal viability is an indicator that all essential components are at or above 0.35 at the terminal step. Terminal minimum state is min(q1,q2,q3) at the terminal step. Time to first failure is the first step at which any essential component falls below 0.35, right-censored at the registered horizon if no failure occurs.

For C1 ablation, the component-specific paired deficit for component j is the matched intact terminal qj minus the ablated terminal qj under the same seed. Topology selectivity is the C2 deficit minus the C3 deficit. The preregistered reciprocal C1-to-C2 edge threshold is epsilon_w=0.25.

Specific rescue effect on C2 is terminal C2 under specific rescue minus terminal C2 under no-rescue C1 ablation. Rescue selectivity is terminal C2 under specific rescue minus terminal C2 under equal-budget irrelevant rescue. Budget diagnostics sum maintenance allocation over components at each step and across the trajectory as required.

344-71.value:
The primary confirmatory analysis uses fixed preregistered estimands, seed-consistency counts and magnitude/noninferiority thresholds rather than ANOVA, regression or primary null-hypothesis significance testing.

H1.1 compares path viability of passive and active architectures across low, medium and high disturbance, with the preregistered graded-demand and 16/20 or 4/20 count criteria. H1.2 compares terminal viability and terminal minimum component state after external-support withdrawal. H1.3 uses paired intact-minus-ablated component deficits to test the reciprocal C1-to-C2 edge and topology-selectivity signature relative to feed-forward structure. H1.4 compares no rescue, specific rescue and equal-budget irrelevant rescue using paired terminal C2 differences. H1.6 applies preregistered noninferiority margins to reciprocal versus brute-force bypass outcomes.

Wilson 95% intervals are reported for viability proportions. Continuous paired effects use paired percentile-bootstrap 95% intervals with 10,000 resamples and fixed analysis RNG seed 20261002. Failure-time summaries are right-censored at the registered horizon and reported descriptively. Only C1 is preregistered as the decisive node-level ablation, so no familywise correction is required for the primary edge test. Any additional node ablations are exploratory.

344-75.value: No outcome-dependent transformation, centering, standardisation or logarithmic transformation is planned. Architecture and condition are represented by fixed categorical identifiers. Seed identity is retained for paired comparisons. Derived variables are calculated exactly as defined above. Values q_i remain on their native [0,1] scale.

344-77.value:
Primary inference uses the frozen Retain/Restrict/Reduce/Suspend/Reject criteria in the attached preregistration record rather than p-value thresholds. Each hypothesis receives a separate verdict. Mixed outcomes are explicitly permitted; for example, H1.3/H1.4 may retain a real reciprocal causal edge and specific rescue while H1.6 reduces the necessity of reciprocal topology if the brute-force bypass is noninferior.

No pooled hierarchy significance test or post-hoc total organisation score will be constructed. Secondary analyses cannot replace a failed primary criterion.

344-79.value:
All technically valid runs from all 20 registered seeds are included. No valid run is removed as an outlier or because it conflicts with the prediction.

A run is excluded from scientific analysis only for preregistered technical invalidity: manifest or referenced-config hash mismatch, unregistered seed, environment validation failure, non-finite numerical state, corrupted required output, or failed provenance/integrity verification. The invalid run and reason remain in the audit trail and the same seed may be rerun after correction.

A valid negative outcome remains scientific evidence and is not classified as an invalid run.

344-81.value: No statistical imputation is planned. Missing required output due to technical failure causes the run to be classified INVALID_RUN and rerun with the same registered seed after documented correction where possible. If decisive evidence cannot be obtained validly, the relevant hypothesis may receive SUSPEND rather than having missing values imputed or ignored.

344-83.value:
Secondary reporting will include per-seed trajectories, maintenance-expenditure diagnostics, component-specific time courses and right-censored failure-time summaries. These analyses help interpret registered effects but do not replace primary decision thresholds.

H1.5 boundary/timescale robustness is explicitly deferred. Additional node ablations, alternative system boundaries, altered temporal resolutions or new bypass architectures arising after inspection of confirmatory outcomes will be labelled exploratory or registered as separate follow-up studies before being used confirmatorily.

344-86.value:
B2 follows the preregistered B1 Gray-Scott driven-pattern baseline (OSF DOI 10.17605/OSF.IO/G3TE5), which established only that sustained non-equilibrium driving can support reproducible persistent spatial organisation within the tested Gray-Scott regime. B2 does not interpret that persistence as self-maintenance. It asks the distinct causal question of whether internally generated processes contribute selectively to preserving operational organisation.

The experiment deliberately includes a strong budget-matched brute-force bypass. Consequently, a result in which reciprocal edges are causally validated but reciprocal topology is unnecessary is an anticipated and scientifically acceptable mixed outcome. The programme is designed to revise or reduce unsupported structure rather than force confirmation of a hierarchy.

H1.5 is not tested in this first B2 study because only one system boundary and one native temporal resolution are implemented. No boundary-robustness or timescale-robustness claim will be inferred retrospectively from this experiment.

A positive B2 result would establish only artificial functional/causal self-maintenance within the registered conditions. Mapping any such mechanism to biological self-maintenance would require a separate cross-domain validation programme.
